title: But What About Natural Talent?
coreMove: Turn a talent claim into an investigation of training history, access, selection, and response before accepting a fixed ceiling.
sourcePressure: The chapter handles the strongest objection: talent and biology matter, but high performance cannot be explained by talent alone because training history, selection effects, support, and response variation distort the story. Frozen sidecar for chapter 8 contains no traceable named figure, study, place, date, or artifact beyond the authors and chapter mechanism; sourceAnchors stays empty rather than inventing one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version either denies talent completely or treats talent as the final explanation.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line

exampleSpecs.domain: junior data analyst compared with a spreadsheet prodigy
exampleSpecs.audience: a worker tempted to make one colleague's speed a fixed verdict
exampleSpecs.stakes: envy can end the search for the templates, macros, and review history behind the gap
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia asks to see the analyst's revision history, finds years of macro notebooks and peer corrections, and chooses one trainable cause before calling the gap talent
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a spreadsheet revision panel open beside a stack of macro notes

exampleSpecs.domain: youth soccer tryout selection after early puberty
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach separating current size from future skill
exampleSpecs.stakes: selection effects could give bigger players more coaching and create the talent story later
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ben reviews tryout notes, separates speed from first-touch decisions, and reserves two training slots for smaller players whose cues improve under coaching
exampleSpecs.firstImage: tryout bibs piled beside a clipboard with height marks

exampleSpecs.domain: music-school entrance auditions and family access
exampleSpecs.audience: an admissions teacher noticing that polish often reflects years of support
exampleSpecs.stakes: a raw student may be denied the coaching that would reveal real response to training
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Etienne compares audition polish with lesson history, adds a callback teaching test, and watches which students improve after one correction
exampleSpecs.firstImage: audition forms stacked beside a practice-room key ring
mustAvoid: access as excuse for no standards

exampleSpecs.domain: software bootcamp admissions using take-home puzzle scores
exampleSpecs.audience: an instructor wary of confusing prior exposure with raw aptitude
exampleSpecs.stakes: selection can reward people who saw the puzzle type before and starve others of training
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Frida groups score sheets by prior coding exposure, adds a taught mini-lesson, and compares improvement rate instead of first score alone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: take-home score sheets warm from a copier tray

exampleSpecs.domain: language accent coaching for adult pronunciation
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult learner who thinks a bad ear is permanent
exampleSpecs.stakes: the label can stop him before testing whether targeted feedback changes one sound
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 12:24 p.m., Diego predicts he cannot hear the vowel difference, then uses a spectrogram and coach cue to see whether three corrected attempts narrow the gap
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two colored vowel bands on a laptop spectrogram

exampleSpecs.domain: math circle puzzle performance after home enrichment
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher deciding how to interpret one child's quick answers
exampleSpecs.stakes: calling one child gifted too soon can change who gets harder problems and feedback
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Aanya solve quickly, then the teacher asks about puzzle exposure at home and gives the group a new puzzle type to compare learning from first feedback
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wooden tangram pieces scattered beside a sign-up sheet

skillTargets: investigate talent claims without denying biology
